$comment: Meridian Launch Systems demo identity manifest (Layer L3). All people are FICTIONAL; no real PII - this file is committed to a PUBLIC repo, so real presenters are added in the portal only and never listed here (CLAUDE.md hard rule 4). UPNs are composed as <userPrincipalNamePrefix>@<domain>; the domain below is a placeholder overridden at apply time via apply-entra.ps1 -Domain (the tenant's real verified domain). Applied by apply-entra.ps1 - idempotent create-if-absent/update.
$appRegistrationsComment: appKey maps a registration to the app it belongs to, using the SAME key infra/bicep/naming.bicep's appKeys uses. It is metadata for callers, not Graph: apply-entra.ps1 reads displayName/signInAudience/notes and ignores everything else. .github/workflows/layer-07-apps.yml resolves each dashboard's Easy Auth client ID by looking the registration up under its appKey and then by its displayName, so the workflow never hardcodes the company prefix (CLAUDE.md) and a renamed registration cannot silently gate the wrong app.
$conditionalAccessComment: THREE policies, and only ONE of them is enforced. ${prefix}-ca-require-mfa-dashboards is state=enabled: it requires MFA for ALL users signing in to the THREE human-facing dashboards (launch-ops, control-tower, compliance) and nothing else, which is the narrowest scope that still covers every place a human signs in to this estate. The other two target includeApplications:[All] - one every admin directory role, one every legacy client - and stay enabledForReportingButNotEnforced: an All/All grant enforced in someone else's tenant is a lockout, not a demo. The two *ByDisplayName keys are NOT Graph fields. Graph wants object ids (appId for applications, group id for groups) which do not exist until this manifest is applied, so apply-entra.ps1 resolves the names it created moments earlier and substitutes them - app registrations are created before CA policies for exactly that reason. An enabled policy MUST exclude a group flagged "breakGlass": true, and apply-entra.ps1 refuses to create or enable it until that group actually holds a cloud-only emergency-access account that is not one of the fictional personas above (docs/runbooks/g0-bootstrap.md item 13, docs/runbooks/layers/L03.md).
$bootstrapAppRegistrationsComment: IDENTITIES THIS LAYER DOES NOT CREATE AND MUST NEVER TRY TO. Every entry is an app registration created by hand at G0, before any pipeline exists, carrying a credential a script cannot mint: a federated credential bound to this repository, or an X.509 certificate. apply-entra.ps1 iterates appRegistrations ONLY and never reads this key - Assert-ManifestSchema enforces that the two arrays are disjoint, because a name appearing in both would have L3 create a credential-less impostor on any tenant where the real one is absent, and V3.1 would go green on it. They are declared here for exactly one reason: L3's V3.1 drift sweep asks whether every ${prefix}-prefixed registration in the tenant is accounted for by a declaration in this repository, and until 2026-09-03 the answer lived in a hardcoded two-name literal inside the audit itself - a second source of truth, in the one file whose job is to have no independent knowledge, that also hardcoded the company prefix (F90's class). Declaring a bootstrap identity here EXEMPTS it from drift and is a deliberate, reviewable act with a diff; it is not a pattern, so an undeclared ${prefix}-anything still fails V3.1. An entry that is ABSENT from the tenant is reported, not failed: a clone that has not run every G0 step is a degrade path, not drift.
$licensingComment: 'licensed' controls which users V3.4 asserts an EMS E5 assignment for; it does NOT assign anything. apply-entra.ps1 assigns no licences at all - it only sets usageLocation, which is a prerequisite for licensing. Assignment itself is a human step in the M365 admin center (g0-bootstrap.md item C10). All five are true while the EMS E5 trial's free seats last; at trial expiry flip the ones you no longer sign in as to false and V3.4 narrows with no code change. A user with the flag absent is treated as licensed, so older manifests audit exactly as before.

groups.description: Flight operations staff - launch-ops app users
Finance - cost dashboards and budget alerts
Emergency access (break-glass) accounts. Excluded from the enforced dashboard MFA policy so a Conditional Access misconfiguration can never lock the tenant's owner out of their own tenant.

Licence-free Copilot Studio authoring rights. Assign this group to the "Copilot Studio authors" tenant setting in the Power Platform admin center (g0 item C5). Without it Copilot Studio offers only the licence-gated Teams fallback, and the standard-harness authoring the demo agent needs is unreachable.
groups.notes: Members are added by hand: the operator who authors the Copilot Studio agent needs this, and which human that is cannot be known by the repo. The GROUP is created here so the 'Copilot Studio authors' tenant setting has something to point at (g0 item C5).

groups.description: Azure SQL Entra administrator. The SQL server takes a GROUP, not a user, as its Entra admin.
groups.notes: Holds the human operator AND the deploy service principal. A single-user admin breaks whichever side is left out: a human-only admin blocks the deployer that applies the schema, a deployer-only admin blocks a human ever querying the database (F84). Neither is a manifest persona, so membership is managed outside this file - the group existed in the tenant and in no manifest until 2026-08-31, which V3.1's drift sweep correctly reported (F92).

appRegistrations.notes: MCP tool server the Copilot Studio agent attaches to (apps/mcp-tools)

Compliance board (apps/compliance). Added by F25: Container Apps Easy Auth on the three human-facing dashboards needs one app registration each, and this was the one the manifest never declared - g0-bootstrap.md's own box said so. Its application (client) id goes into the MLS_COMPLIANCE_CLIENT_ID variable; the launch-ops and control-tower registrations above now feed MLS_LAUNCH_OPS_CLIENT_ID and MLS_CONTROL_TOWER_CLIENT_ID the same way. Each app's Easy Auth redirect URI is https://<that app's ingress fqdn>/.auth/login/aad/callback, which only exists after L7 - see docs/runbooks/layers/L03.md.

bootstrapAppRegistrations.notes: The OIDC deploy identity, federated to this repository's environments and holding no stored cloud secret. It is the identity that APPLIES this manifest, so it cannot be declared in it: it holds Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy, which covers only the registrations it created itself.

The read-only audit identity - Reader, Directory.Read.All, Policy.Read.All. It is the identity RUNNING the audit that reads this file. It also carries its own X.509 certificate (MLS_VERIFIER_CERT_BASE64) for the L4 Security & Compliance audit.

Security & Compliance app-only identity for L4's label taxonomy. Carries a hand-minted X.509 certificate (PURVIEW_CERT_BASE64), Exchange.ManageAsApp granted directly through Graph, and membership of Compliance Administrator - all because Security & Compliance PowerShell has no federated auth path, which is why CLAUDE.md hard rule 5 permits the certificate at all. Its client id is the PURVIEW_APP_ID variable on the demo environment. Absent on a tenant that has not run step 11c, where L4 falls back to running under a human login (F43) - a degrade path, not drift.
